  89+ 0000              ; Sets IYH to sign bits, bit 7 = x, bit 6 = y bit 5 = z
  90+ 0000              SetIYHToSignBits:       MACRO
  91+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_ZSGNOFFSET)   ; get Z sign
  92+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  93+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  94+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
  95+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_YSGNOFFSET)   ; get Y sign
  96+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  97+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Z into IYH bit 6
  98+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  99+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 100+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_XSGNOFFSET)   ; get X sign
 101+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
 102+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Y into IYH bit 6 and Z into IYH bit 5
 103+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 104+ 0000                                      ENDM

 271+ 6070              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 272+ 6070              ; Laser, once a main loop. Times are 50 Hz frames of FrameCounter16 (the interrupt's count, stopped while paused), so a
 273+ 6070              ; pulse lasts as long however fast the loop runs. Like Z-Police's game clock (clock_step): dt = the frames since the last
 274+ 6070              ; update (at most LaserMaxFrames, so a stall doesn't jump), and each state's end is a frame number, compared by 16 bit
 275+ 6070              ; subtraction so it works across the counter's wrap.
 276+ 6070              ;   LaserReady  fire held (LaserFireHeld, from the front view's keys) starts a burst of CurrLaserPulseRate pulses,
 277+ 6070              ;               or with a rate of 0 a beam
 278+ 6070              ;   LaserOn     a pulse, CurrLaserPulseOnTime frames; a beam stays on while fire is held
 279+ 6070              ;   LaserOff    CurrLaserPulseOffTime frames between a burst's pulses
 280+ 6070              ;   LaserRest   CurrLaserPulseRest frames after a burst (or a beam) before the next
 281+ 6070              ; Out: LaserBeamOn (the sprite), LaserHitDamage (what a ship in the sights takes this loop: a pulse's damage when it
 282+ 6070              ; starts, a beam's for each frame it was on), energy drained and heat added for each frame on, the gun cooled for each
 283+ 6070              ; frame off. LaserFireHeld is cleared: the keys set it again each loop while fire is held.
 284+ 6070              LaserReady              equ 0
 285+ 6070              LaserOn                 equ 1
 286+ 6070              LaserOff                equ 2
 287+ 6070              LaserRest               equ 3
 288+ 6070              LaserMaxFrames          equ 8

  86+ 63BC              ; hl -> 9 byte position (x, y, z each lo, hi, sign). Returns carry set if the object is within 1.0 of us on every axis.
  87+ 63BC              ; The integer part of each S15.8 axis is the sign byte bits 0-6 (upper) and the hi byte (lower); an axis is far enough
  88+ 63BC              ; away if the upper byte is non zero or the lower byte is > 1, and one far axis is enough to allow the warp.
  89+ 63BC 06 03        WarpIsObjectClose:      ld      b,3

  92+ 63C0 23                                   inc     hl                                      ; hl -> sign byte (integer upper byte)
  93+ 63C1 FE 02                                cp      2
  94+ 63C3 D0                                   ret     nc                                      ; lower byte > 1 so far enough, carry clear
  95+ 63C4 7E                                   ld      a,(hl)
  96+ 63C5 E6 7F                                and     SignMask8Bit                            ; also clears carry
  97+ 63C7 C0                                   ret     nz                                      ; upper byte non zero so far enough
  98+ 63C8 23                                   inc     hl                                      ; next axis lo byte
  99+ 63C9 10 F3                                djnz    .AxisLoop

 189+ 6E04              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 190+ 6E04              ; DrawSunDistance / DrawPlanetDistance / DrawStationDistance: print the integer part of the distance to the sun, planet
 191+ 6E04              ; and space station on layer 2 to the right of their compass sprites.
 192+ 6E04              ; The compass sprites sit in the left border (sprite x 0-33, top y = Sun/Planet/StationCompassTLY, layer 2 is offset by
 193+ 6E04              ; 32,32 from sprite coordinates), so the text goes at the left of the 3D view, centred on each compass where possible.
 194+ 6E04              ; That area is cleared every frame, so these are called every frame from the main loop rather than from UpdateConsole,
 195+ 6E04              ; which only runs on console refresh frames.
 196+ 6E04              ; Distance ~= max + 3/8 (mid + min) of |x|, |y|, |z| (within about +13% / -3%), using the integer part of each
 197+ 6E04              ; S15.8 position (sign byte bits 0-6 and the hi byte), so it fits 16 bits (max 57341)
 198+ 6E04              DistanceCol             equ 4
 199+ 6E04              SunDistanceRow          equ 2                                       ; sun compass centre is above layer 2, so top text row
 200+ 6E04              PlanetDistanceRow       equ PlanetCompassTLY + 17 - 32 - 4          ; compass centre (top + 17) in layer 2 rows, less half a character

1196+ 7625              ; Radar edge markers: when the sun, planet or space station is outside the scanner range in X or Z (|x| or |z| >= 64,
1197+ 7625              ; the same limit the blips use, y is ignored) a dot is put on the scanner outline in its direction. The direction is the
1198+ 7625              ; one a blip would use (column = x, row = z / 4) and the ray is stepped out a row at a time until it reaches the outline.
1199+ 7625              ; The outline is not a true ellipse so its half widths are tabled, measured from the console image: columns 59-196,
1200+ 7625              ; rows 155-190, centre 127.5, 172.5 (left and right are symmetric about it)
1201+ 7625              RadarEdgeRowAbove       equ 172                         ; k rows up from here for objects in front (z +ve)
1202+ 7625              RadarEdgeRowBelow       equ 173                         ; k rows down from here for objects behind (z -ve)
1203+ 7625              RadarEdgeColRight       equ 128                         ; w columns right from here for x +ve
1204+ 7625              RadarEdgeColLeft        equ 127                         ; w columns left from here for x -ve
1205+ 7625              RadarEdgeRows           equ 18                          ; k = 0..17
1206+ 7625 44 44 43 43  RadarEdgeUp:            DB  68,68,67,67,66,65,64,62,60,58,56,53,50,46,42,36,29,19   ; half width at row 172 - k

1206+ 7635 1D 13

   3+ 8097              ; A REAL_HARDWARE build uses DMA+ fill mode: no reads, so twice as fast (Documentation/ZXNDDMA.md)
   4+ 8097 83 C3 C7 CB  memfill        		DB DMA_DISABLE,  DMA_RESET, DMA_RESET_PORT_A_TIMING, DMA_RESET_PORT_B_TIMING

   1+ 9530              ;Calculate A = arctan(P / Q)
   2+ 9530              ; This finds the angle in the right-angled triangle where the opposite side to angle A is length P and the adjacent side to angle A has
   3+ 9530              ; length Q, so:  tan(A) = P / Q
   4+ 9530              ;
   5+ 9530              ; The result in A is an integer representing the angle in radians. The routine returns values in the range 0 to 128,  (or 0 to PI radians).
   6+ 9530 3A 33 81     ARCTAN:                 ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set T1 = P EOR Q, which will have the sign of P * Q
   7+ 9533 21 5F 82                             ld      hl,varQ                     ; EOR Q
   8+ 9536 AE                                   xor     (hl)                        ; .
   9+ 9537 32 30 81                             ld      (varT1),a                   ; STA T1
  10+ 953A 3A 5F 82                             ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDA Q                  \ If Q = 0, jump to AR2 to return a right angle
  11+ 953D A7                                   and     a                           ; BEQ AR2
  12+ 953E CA 80 95                             jp      z, .AR2                     ; .
  13+ 9541 CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A                  \ Set Q = |Q| * 2 (this is a quick way of clearing the
  14+ 9543 32 5F 82                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; STA Q                  \ sign bit, and we don't need to shift right again as we only ever use this value in the division with |P| * 2, which we set next)
  15+ 9546 3A 33 81                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set A = |P| * 2
  16+ 9549 CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A
  17+ 954B 32 33 81                             ld      (varP),a
  18+ 954E 21 5F 82                             ld      hl,varQ
  19+ 9551 BE                                   cp      (hl)                        ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, i.e. |P| > |Q|, jump to AR1 to swap P
  20+ 9552 D2 64 95                             jp      nc, .AR1                    ; BCS AR1                \ and Q around, so we can still use the lookup table
  21+ 9555 CD 8C 95                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table:  A = arctan(A / Q)  = arctan(|P / Q|)
  22+ 9558                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag so the SBC instruction in AR3 will be correct, should we jump there
  22+ 9558 B7          >                        or a
  23+ 9559 4F           .AR4:                   ld      c,a                         ; as we have to use a we use c as a temp, we can't push af as we would loose flags on pop
  24+ 955A 3A 30 81                             ld      a,(varT1)                   ; LDX T1                 \ If T1 is negative, i.e. P and Q have different signs,
  25+ 955D 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  26+ 955E A7                                   and     a                           ; BMI AR3                \ jump down to AR3 to return arctan(-|P / Q|)
  27+ 955F 79                                   ld      a,c                         ; .                      \ we need to get a back before jump
  28+ 9560 FA 83 95                             jp      m, .AR3                     ; .
  29+ 9563 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Otherwise P and Q have the same sign, so our result is correct and we can return from the subroutine
  30+ 9564              ; We want to calculate arctan(t) where |t| > 1, so we can use the calculation described in the documentation for the ACT table, i.e. 64 - arctan(1 / t)
  31+ 9564              ; In the 6502 verion it works with A already being P but we will fetch it
  32+ 9564 3A 5F 82     .AR1:                   ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDX Q                  \ Swap the values in Q and P, using the fact that we
  33+ 9567 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  34+ 9568 3A 33 81                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; STA Q                  \ called AR1 with A = P
  35+ 956B 32 5F 82                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; .
  36+ 956E 78                                   ld      a,b                         ; TXA                    \ This also sets A = P (which now contains the original argument |Q|)
  37+ 956F 32 33 81                             ld      (varP),a                    ; STX P                  \
  38+ 9572 CD 8C 95                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table: A = arctan(A / Q) = arctan(|Q / P|) = arctan(1 / |P / Q|)
  39+ 9575 32 7B 82                             ld      (varT),a                    ; STA T                  \ Set T = 64 - T, we use B as T (its not really that)
  40+ 9578 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; its actually t = a, a = 64-a
  41+ 9579 3E 40                                ld      a,64                        ; LDA #64 What is going on here is t = result
  42+ 957B                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SBC T                            a = 64- result
  42+ 957B B7          >                        or a
  43+ 957C 98                                   sbc     a,b                         ; .

  45+ 9580              ; If we get here then Q = 0, so tan(A) = infinity and A is a right angle, or 0.25 of a circle. We allocate 255 to a full circle, so we should return 63 for a right angle
  46+ 9580 3E 3F        .AR2:                   ld      a,63                        ; LDA #63                \ Set A to 63, to represent a right angle
  47+ 9582 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine

  52+ 9589 B7          >                        or a

  54+ 958B C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  55+ 958C              ; This routine fetches arctan(A / Q) from the ACT table, so A will be set to an integer in the range 0 to 31 that represents an angle from 0 to 45 degrees (or 0 to \ PI / 4 radians)
  56+ 958C              ARS1:                   MMUSelectMathsTables
  56+ 958C ED 91 50 63 >                     nextreg MathsTablesMMU,    BankMathsTables
  57+ 9590 CD 9F 07                             call    Amul256DivQ                 ; JSR LL28               \ Call LL28 to calculate: R = 256 * A / Q
  58+ 9593 3A 60 82                             ld      a,(varR)                    ; LDA R                  \ Set X = R / 8
  59+ 9596 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \       = 32 * A / Q
  60+ 9598 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \
  61+ 959A CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \ so X has the value t * 32 where t = A / Q, which is
  62+ 959C 21 C3 95                             ld      hl,ACT                      ; TAX                    \ what we need to look up values in the ACT table

  64+ 95A1 7E                                   ld      a,(hl)                      ;                        \   A = value in ACT + X = value in ACT + (32 * A / Q)= arctan(A / Q)

   1+ 97B2              baddll38:				;.LL38	\ -> &4812 \ BADD(S)A=R+Q(SA) \ byte add (subtract)   (Sign S)A = R + Q*(Sign from A^S)
   2+ 97B2              SAEquSRPlusAQ:
   3+ 97B2              ; Calculate the following between sign-magnitude numbers:
   4+ 97B2              ;   (S A) = (S R) + (A Q)
   5+ 97B2              ; where the sign bytes only contain the sign bits, not magnitudes.
   6+ 97B2              ; note goes wrong at <-127 >128 so need 16 bit version
   7+ 97B2              ; so need to fix the issue with carry flag not returning a fault correctly
   8+ 97B2              LL38:
   9+ 97B2              ; calculation table
  10+ 97B2              ;   R     Q    Op            Sign calc
  11+ 97B2              ;	10    5    Add           +    sign same add R sign
  12+ 97B2              ;   -10   5    ABS Sub       -    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  13+ 97B2              ;   10   -5    ABS sub       +    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  14+ 97B2              ;	-10  -5    ABS Add       -    sign same add R sign
  15+ 97B2              ;   5    10    Add           +    sign same add R sign
  16+ 97B2              ;   -5   10    Swap ABS SUB  +    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB Q sign
  17+ 97B2              ;   5    -10   swap ABS Sub  -    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB R sign
  18+ 97B2              ;   -5   -10   ABS  add      -    sign same add R sign
  19+ 97B2
  20+ 97B2              ;   -10   5    ABS Sub       -    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  21+ 97B2              ;   10   -5    ABS sub       +    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  22+ 97B2              ;   -5   10    Swap ABS SUB  +    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB Q sign
  23+ 97B2              ;   5    -10   swap ABS Sub  -    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB R sign
  24+ 97B2
  25+ 97B2
  26+ 97B2              ; Calculate sign for Q from A and varS
  27+ 97B2 21 61 82     	ld		hl,varS							;
  28+ 97B5 AE           	xor		(hl)							;  EOR &83		\ S	\ sign of operator is A xor S
  29+ 97B6 FA C1 97     	jp		m,.LL39Subtraction  			; if signs are different then we have subtraction
  30+ 97B9 3A 5F 82     	ld		a,(varQ)						; Q	\ else addition, S already correct
  31+ 97BC 21 60 82     	ld		hl,varR
  32+ 97BF 86           	add		a,(hl)							; a = Q + R
  33+ 97C0 C9           	ret										; Done carry set if overflow
  34+ 97C1              .LL39Subtraction:							; 1 byte subtraction (S)A = R-Q
  35+ 97C1 3A 60 82     	ld		a,(varR)						; a = R
  36+ 97C4 21 5F 82     	ld		hl,varQ                         ; Q
  37+ 97C7              ;--	JumpIfALTMemHLusng LL39SwapSubtraction	; if a < (hl) then do LL39SwapSubtraction
  38+ 97C7              	ClearCarryFlag                          ; we need to not use carry (6502 is different that it uses the compliement)
  38+ 97C7 B7          >                        or a
  39+ 97C8 9E           	sbc		a,(hl)							; A = R - Q which as R >= Q will always be a positive result
  40+ 97C9 38 01            jr      c,.LL39SignCorrection
  41+ 97CB              ;--    jr      a,.LL39ResultZero
  42+ 97CB              ;--   JumpIfNegative LL39SignCorrection		; if there was underflow we have to correct sign
  43+ 97CB              ;--	or		a								; Clear carry flag to say result is correct
  44+ 97CB C9           	ret
  45+ 97CC              .LL39SignCorrection:
  46+ 97CC FE 00            cp      0                               ; if its 0 then neg will affect flag so we just zero result to save compute
  47+ 97CE 28 0E            jr      z,.LL39ResultZero
  48+ 97D0 ED 44            neg                                     ; flip A 2'c value to positive
  49+ 97D2 08           	ex		af,af'							; save A temporarily
  50+ 97D3 3A 61 82     	ld		a,(varS)						; Flip Sign bit in varS
  51+ 97D6 EE 80        	xor		$80							    ;
  52+ 97D8 32 61 82     	ld		(varS),a                        ; flip sign bit of a
  53+ 97DB 08           	ex		af,af'                          ; get back a which is the result
  54+ 97DC                  ClearCarryFlag                          ; clear carry as NEG instrunction sets it for non zero
  54+ 97DC B7          >                        or a
  55+ 97DD C9           	ret
  56+ 97DE              .LL39ResultZero:
  57+ 97DE 32 61 82         ld      (varS),a                        ; a is zero at this stage so set sign as well
  58+ 97E1                  ClearCarryFlag                          ; clear carry
  58+ 97E1 B7          >                        or a
  59+ 97E2 C9               ret
  60+ 97E3              ;--LL39SwapSubtraction:
  61+ 97E3              ;--	push	bc
  62+ 97E3              ;--	ld		b,a
  63+ 97E3              ;--	ld		a,(hl)
  64+ 97E3              ;--	sub		b
  65+ 97E3              ;--	pop		bc
  66+ 97E3              ;--	ex		af,af'							; do we flip here or negate. i think its flip as its overflowed unsigned
  67+ 97E3              ;--	ld		a,(varS)
  68+ 97E3              ;--	xor		$80
  69+ 97E3              ;--	ld		(varS),a
  70+ 97E3              ;--	ex		af,af'
  71+ 97E3              ;--	ret

 171+ A2BC C1           .NormalError:  	        pop	bc	; don't pop into A, return with error code

 175+ A2C0
 176+ A2C0              ; *******************************************************************************************************
 177+ A2C0              ; Function:	Save a whole file into memory	(confirmed working on real machine)
 178+ A2C0              ; In:		hl = file name
 179+ A2C0              ;		    ix = address to save from
 180+ A2C0              ;		    bc = size
 181+ A2C0              ; *******************************************************************************************************
 182+ A2C0 CD 4D A2     FileSave:	            call    GetDefaultDrive		; need to do this each time?!?!?
 183+ A2C3 C5 DD E5                             push	bc,,ix   			; store size& save address
 184+ A2C6 E5 DD E1                             ld      ix,hl               ; get name into ix
 185+ A2C9 06 0C                                ld      b,FA_OVERWRITE		; mode open for writing
 186+ A2CB CD 60 A2                             call    fOpen
 187+ A2CE 38 1A                                jr	    c,.error_opening	; carry set? so there was an error opening and A=error code
 188+ A2D0 FE 00                                cp	    0			        ; was file handle 0?
 189+ A2D2 28 16                                jr	    z,.error_opening	; of so there was an error opening.
 190+ A2D4 DD E1 C1                             pop	    bc,,ix			    ; get lenght and save address back
 191+ A2D7 F5                                   push	af			        ; remember handle
 192+ A2D8 CD 73 A2                             call	fWrite			    ; read data from A to address IX of length BC
 193+ A2DB 38 05                                jr	c,.error
 194+ A2DD F1                                   pop	af			            ; get handle back
 195+ A2DE CD 7D A2                             call	fClose			    ; close file
 196+ A2E1 C9                                   ret
 197+ A2E2 C1           .error:                 pop     bc                  ; b = handle (pushed with af), the stack is balanced again
 198+ A2E3 F5                                   push    af                  ; keep the error code and carry
 199+ A2E4 78                                   ld      a,b                 ; close the file
 200+ A2E5 CD 7D A2                             call    fClose              ; .
 201+ A2E8 F1                                   pop     af                  ; carry set, a = error code
 202+ A2E9 C9                                   ret
 203+ A2EA              ;
 204+ A2EA              ; On error, display error code an lock up so we can see it
 205+ A2EA              ;
 206+ A2EA DD E1 C1     .error_opening:         pop	bc,,ix                  ; don't pop a, need error code
 207+ A2ED C9                                   ret

 143+ E0C6              ; "asm_l2_320_row_bank_select"
 144+ E0C6              ; HL (unsinged) = x column of pixel line from left, uses this to define bank
 145+ E0C6              ; 0-  63                    Bank 1
 146+ E0C6              ; 64- 127                   Bank 2
 147+ E0C6              ; 128 - 191                 Bank 3
 148+ E0C6              ; 192 - 255                 Bank 4
 149+ E0C6              ; 256 - 321                 Bank 5
 150+ E0C6              ; outputs h with the correct column number adjusted for bank selection
 151+ E0C6 7C           asm_l2_320_col_bank_select: ld      a,h
 152+ E0C7 A7                                       and     a

 154+ E0CB 7D                                       ld      a,l
 155+ E0CC E6 C0                                    and     %11000000                       ; if upper 2 bits are set then must be bank 4
 156+ E0CE CA D6 E0                                 jp      z,.NotBank4
 157+ E0D1 FE C0                                    cp      %11000000
 158+ E0D3 CA 3B E1                                 jp      z,.Bank4
 159+ E0D6 7D           .NotBank4:                  ld      a,l                             ; try again with original number

 161+ E0DA C2 1C E1                                 jp      nz,.Bank3
 162+ E0DD ED 27 40                                 test    %01000000                       ; if 64 to 127 then bank 2
 163+ E0E0 C2 FD E0                                 jp      nz,.Bank2

  48+ ECFE              InstrDECIY              equ $2B
  49+ ECFE              InstrINCIY              equ $23

  51+ ECFE              ;--- Swaps point 1 and point 2 around (i.e x1 y1 <--> x2 y2)
  52+ ECFE 2A E5 EC     SwapCoords:             ld      hl,(y1)                         ;       then swap point 1 and point 2
  53+ ED01 ED 5B E9 EC                          ld      de,(y2)                         ;       .
  54+ ED05 ED 53 E5 EC                          ld      (y1),de                         ;       .

  59+ ED17 22 E7 EC                             ld      (x2),hl                         ;       .

  61+ ED1B
  62+ ED1B              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  63+ ED1B              ; l2_draw_6502_line - clip and draw a line in the Layer 2 upper two thirds (256x128, rows 0-63 bank 0, rows 64-127 bank 1)
  64+ ED1B              ; In : x1,y1,x2,y2 16 bit signed, nominally -1024..+1024 (any value within +/-2047 is safe)
  65+ ED1B              ;      colour from line_gfx_colour, Layer 2 code bank paged in (MMUSelectLayer2)
  66+ ED1B              ; Out: carry set   - line wholly outside the window, nothing drawn
  67+ ED1B              ;      carry clear - line drawn, x1,y1,x2,y2 hold the clipped end points (high bytes 0)
  68+ ED1B              ;      AF, BC, DE, HL, AF' destroyed, IX and IY preserved
  69+ ED1B              ; y1 = y2           horizontal, clamped without any maths, P1 = P2 plots a single pixel, long spans are a DMA fill
  70+ ED1B              ; x1 = x2           vertical, clamped without any maths, column fill split at the bank 0/1 boundary
  71+ ED1B              ; otherwise         Cohen-Sutherland outcodes for trivial accept/reject, edge intersections via 12x12 multiply and
  72+ ED1B              ;                   24/16 divide (rounded), then the clipped line is re-checked for pixel/horz/vert before an 8 bit Bresenham
  73+ ED1B              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  74+ ED1B              L2L_OC_LEFT_BIT         equ     0
  75+ ED1B              L2L_OC_RIGHT_BIT        equ     1
  76+ ED1B              L2L_OC_TOP_BIT          equ     2
  77+ ED1B              L2L_OC_BOTTOM_BIT       equ     3
  78+ ED1B              L2L_OC_LEFT             equ     1 << L2L_OC_LEFT_BIT            ; x < 0
  79+ ED1B              L2L_OC_RIGHT            equ     1 << L2L_OC_RIGHT_BIT           ; x > 255
  80+ ED1B              L2L_OC_TOP              equ     1 << L2L_OC_TOP_BIT             ; y < 0
  81+ ED1B              L2L_OC_BOTTOM           equ     1 << L2L_OC_BOTTOM_BIT          ; y > 127
  82+ ED1B              L2L_CLIP_MAX_X          equ     255
  83+ ED1B              L2L_CLIP_MAX_Y          equ     127
  84+ ED1B              L2L_CLIP_MAX_PASSES     equ     8                               ; Cohen-Sutherland needs at most 4, guards against a rounding loop
  85+ ED1B              L2L_DMA_MIN             equ     20                              ; spans this long or longer use DMA, the program upload costs ~20 pixels of CPU loop
  86+ ED1B              L2L_OPCODE_INC_L        equ     $2C
  87+ ED1B              L2L_OPCODE_DEC_L        equ     $2D
  88+ ED1B              L2L_DMA_WR1_FIXED_TIMED equ     $64                             ; WR1 port A memory, fixed address, timing byte follows
  89+ ED1B              L2L_DMA_WR2_INC_TIMED   equ     $50                             ; WR2 port B memory, incrementing, timing byte follows
  90+ ED1B              L2L_DMA_CYCLE_2T        equ     $02                             ; timing byte, 2 T state cycle length
  91+ ED1B
  92+ ED1B 00           L2LClipPasses           DB      0
  93+ ED1C 00           L2LDx                   DB      0
  94+ ED1D 00           L2LDy                   DB      0
  95+ ED1E 00 00        L2LOrigX1               DW      0                               ; original line, all clip intersections are taken from this
  96+ ED20 00 00        L2LOrigY1               DW      0
  97+ ED22 00 00        L2LOrigDx               DW      0
  98+ ED24 00 00        L2LOrigDy               DW      0
  99+ ED26 00 00        L2LOrigAbsDx            DW      0
 100+ ED28 00 00        L2LOrigAbsDy            DW      0

 108+ ED33 50 02                                DB      L2L_DMA_WR2_INC_TIMED,   L2L_DMA_CYCLE_2T

# file opened: l2_draw_line_v2.asm
   1+ F0F7              ; ******************************************************************************
   2+ F0F7              ;
   3+ F0F7              ;	Draw a pixel line from (x0,y0) defined in (COORDS) - the current plot
   4+ F0F7              ;	coordinate, to the relative distance points (x0+x,y0+y).
   5+ F0F7              ;
   6+ F0F7              ;	Design & programming by Gunther Strube,	Copyright (C) InterLogic 1995
   7+ F0F7              ;
   8+ F0F7              ;	The (COORDS+0)	pointer contains the current y coordinate, (COORDS+1) the
   9+ F0F7              ;	current x coordinate. The main program should reset the (COORDS) variables
  10+ F0F7              ;	before using line drawing.
  11+ F0F7              ;
  12+ F0F7              ;	The routine checks the range of specified coordinates which is the
  13+ F0F7              ;	boundaries of the graphics area (256x64	pixels).
  14+ F0F7              ;	If a boundary error occurs the routine exits automatically.	This may be
  15+ F0F7              ;	useful if you are trying to draw a line longer than allowed. Only the
  16+ F0F7              ;	visible part will be drawn.
  17+ F0F7              ;
  18+ F0F7              ;	The hardware graphics memory is organized as (0,0) in the top left corner.
  19+ F0F7              ;
  20+ F0F7              ;	The plot routine is	defined by an address pointer	in IX.
  21+ F0F7              ;
  22+ F0F7              ;	IN:	HL =	move	relative x horisontal points (maximum +/- 255).
  23+ F0F7              ;		DE =	move	relative y vertical	points (maximum +/-	255).
  24+ F0F7              ;		IX =	pointer to plot routine that uses HL = (x,y)	of plot coordinate.
  25+ F0F7              ;
  26+ F0F7              ;	OUT:	None.
  27+ F0F7              ;
  28+ F0F7              ;	Registers	used	by routine:
  29+ F0F7              ;		   N	:	B, loop counter
  30+ F0F7              ;		   i	:	line	balance variable
  31+ F0F7              ;		   x	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  32+ F0F7              ;		   y	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  33+ F0F7              ;	  (x0,y0)	:	(h,l)
  34+ F0F7              ;	  direc_x	:	d, horisontal step increment
  35+ F0F7              ;	  direc_y	:	e, vertical step increment
  36+ F0F7              ;		 ddx	:	b, horisontal step increment
  37+ F0F7              ;		 ddy	:	c, vertical step increment
  38+ F0F7              ;
  39+ F0F7              ;		DE, A work registers.
  40+ F0F7              ;
  41+ F0F7              ; The algorithm in pseudo-code:
  42+ F0F7              ;
  43+ F0F7              ;	direc_x =	SGN x: direc_y	= SGN y
  44+ F0F7              ;	x = ABS x: y =	ABS y
  45+ F0F7              ;
  46+ F0F7              ;	if x	>= y
  47+ F0F7              ;		if x+y=0 then return
  48+ F0F7              ;		H = x
  49+ F0F7              ;		L = y
  50+ F0F7              ;		ddx = direc_x
  51+ F0F7              ;		ddy = 0
  52+ F0F7              ;	else
  53+ F0F7              ;		H = y
  54+ F0F7              ;		L = x
  55+ F0F7              ;		ddx = 0
  56+ F0F7              ;		ddy = direc_y
  57+ F0F7              ;	endif
  58+ F0F7              ;
  59+ F0F7              ;	B = H
  60+ F0F7              ;	i = INT(B/2)
  61+ F0F7              ;	FOR N=B TO 1 STEP -1
  62+ F0F7              ;		i = i + L
  63+ F0F7              ;		if i	< H
  64+ F0F7              ;			ix =	ddx
  65+ F0F7              ;			iy =	ddy
  66+ F0F7              ;		else
  67+ F0F7              ;			i = i - H
  68+ F0F7              ;			ix =	direc_x
  69+ F0F7              ;			iy =	direc_y
  70+ F0F7              ;		endif
  71+ F0F7              ;		x0 =	x0 +	ix
  72+ F0F7              ;		y0 =	y0 +	iy
  73+ F0F7              ;		plot	(x0,y0)
  74+ F0F7              ;	NEXT	N
  75+ F0F7              ;
  76+ F0F7              ;
  77+ F0F7              ;	Registers	changed after return:
  78+ F0F7              ;		..BCDEHL/IXIY/af......	same
  79+ F0F7              ;		AF....../..../..bcdehl	different
  80+ F0F7              ;
  81+ F0F7 00 00        line_gfx_coords         dw  0
  82+ F0F9
  83+ F0F9              LineHLtoDE:
  84+ F0F9 7C           TestMaxY:               ld	a,h ; were h = y or l = y?
  85+ F0FA FE C0                                cp	192

 208+ F1A0              ; ******************************************************************************
 209+ F1A0              ;
 210+ F1A0              ;	SGN (Signum value) of 16	bit signed integer.
 211+ F1A0              ;
 212+ F1A0              ;	IN:		HL =	integer
 213+ F1A0              ;	OUT:		A = result: 0,1,-1 (if zero, positive, negative)
 214+ F1A0              ;
 215+ F1A0              ;	Registers	changed after return:
 216+ F1A0              ;	..BCDEHL/IXIY	same
 217+ F1A0              ;	AF....../....	different
 218+ F1A0              ;

 220+ F1A1 B5                                   or	l
 221+ F1A2 C8                                   ret	z				; integer	is zero, return 0...

 223+ F1A5 20 03                                jr	nz, negative_int
 224+ F1A7 3E 01                                ld	a,1
 225+ F1A9 C9                                   ret
 226+ F1AA 3E FF        negative_int:		    ld	a,-1
 227+ F1AC C9                                   ret

 229+ F1AD
 230+ F1AD              ; ******************************************************************************
 231+ F1AD              ;
 232+ F1AD              ;	ABS (Absolute value) of 16 bit signed integer.
 233+ F1AD              ;
 234+ F1AD              ;	IN:		HL =	integer
 235+ F1AD              ;	OUT:		HL =	converted	integer
 236+ F1AD              ;
 237+ F1AD              ;	Registers	changed after return:
 238+ F1AD              ;	A.BCDE../IXIY	same
 239+ F1AD              ;	.F....HL/....	different
 240+ F1AD              ;
 241+ F1AD CB 7C        absValue:			    bit	7,h
 242+ F1AF C8                                   ret	z				; integer	is positive...

 768  E00F              GetShipBank3Id:         MGetShipBankId ShipBankTable3
 768  E00F 06 00       >                        ld      b,0
 768  E011 4F          >                        ld      c,a                                 ; c= original ship id
 768  E012 CB 3F       >.ShiftLoop:             srl     a
 768  E014 CB 3F       >                        srl     a
 768  E016 CB 3F       >                        srl     a
 768  E018 CB 3F       >                        srl     a                                   ; divide by 16
 768  E01A 47          >                        ld      b,a                                 ; b = bank nbr
 768  E01B 79          >                        ld      a,c
 768  E01C 50          >                        ld      d,b
 768  E01D 1E 10       >                        ld      e,16
 768  E01F ED 30       >                        mul                                         ; de = 16 * bank number (max is about 15 banks)
 768  E021 93          >                        sub     e                                   ; a= actual model id now
 768  E022 50          >.SelectedBank:          ld      d,b                                 ; save current bank number
 768  E023 47          >                        ld      b,a                                 ; b = adjusted ship nbr
 768  E024 7A          >                        ld      a,d                                 ; a = bank number
 768  E025             >;.. Now b = bank and a = adjusted ship nbr
 768  E025 21 62 E0    >                        ld      hl,ShipBankTable3                        ; a= bank index
 768  E028 ED 31       >                        add     hl,a
 768  E02A ED 31       >                        add     hl,a
 768  E02C 7E          >                        ld      a,(hl)                              ; a = actual bank now
 768  E02D             >                        ClearCarryFlag
 768  E02D B7          >                        or a
 768  E02E C9          >                        ret

 204+ E0BC              ; Creates a 32x32 sprite based on first sprite number and pattern, then goes:
 205+ E0BC              ;    Spr,   pattern     spr+1, pattern+1
 206+ E0BC              ;    Spr+1, pattern+2   spr+3, pattern+3
 207+ E0BC              ; " sprite_big BC = row, hl= col D = sprite nbr , E= , pattern"
 208+ E0BC              ; note, BC and HL must be in correct range else they will mess up other byte's attributes, not masked for speed
 209+ E0BC              ; note this is based on full screen sprites including writing to border
 210+ E0BC              ; Currently can not get realtive sprites to work so will brute force it.
 211+ E0BC 7B           sprite_4x4:                 ld      a,e                                                         ; prep upper 2 bits as we will
 212+ E0BD F6 C0                                    or      %11000000                                                   ; Enable visible and 5th byte
 213+ E0BF 5F                                       ld      e,a                                                         ; a now holds value to use for anchor
 214+ E0C0 7A           .SetAnchor:                 ld      a,d
 214+ E0C1 ED 92 34       nextreg   SPRITE_PORT_INDEX_REGISTER,a        ; set up sprite id
 215+ E0C4 7D                                       ld      a,l
 215+ E0C5 ED 92 35       nextreg   SPRITE_PORT_ATTR0_REGISTER,a        ; Set up lower x cc
 216+ E0C8 79                                       ld      a,c
 216+ E0C9 ED 92 36       nextreg   SPRITE_PORT_ATTR1_REGISTER,a        ; Set up lower y cc
 217+ E0CC 7C                                       ld      a,h

 218+ E0D0 7B                                       ld      a,e

 154++C0BE
 155++C0BE              ; UBnkaiatkecm
 156++C0BE              ; Bit	                Description
 157++C0BE              ; 7 -                   AI Enabled Flag
 158++C0BE              ; 6 -                   Ship Visible = ShipOnScreen/NotCloaked (cleared or set by check visible or cloaking override)
 159++C0BE              ; 5 -                   Ship is exploding if set, note if its a missile and one already equeued this will have to linger
 160++C0BE              ;                       linger can be done by not erasing ship unit missile equeue handled
 161++C0BE              ; 4 -                   Ship marked as exploded, cleared once aknowledged then bit 5 takes over and UBnKCloudCounter
 162++C0BE              ; 3 -                   Display state - Plot as a Dot
 163++C0BE              ; 2 -                   Nbr of Missiles bit 2
 164++C0BE              ; 1 -                   Nbr of Missiles bit 1
 165++C0BE              ; 0 -                   ECM present flag
 166++C0BE              ; ShipNewBitsAddr (in blueprint)
 167++C0BE              ;Bit	                Description
 168++C0BE              ;#0	Trader flag         * 0 = not a trader  * 1 = trader
 169++C0BE              ;                       80% of traders are peaceful and mind their own business plying their trade between the planet and space station, but 20% of them moonlight as bounty hunters (see bit #1)
 170++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are traders: Escape pod, Shuttle, Transporter, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Worm
 171++C0BE              ;#1 Bounty hunter flag  * 0 = not a bounty hunter* 1 = bounty hunter
 172++C0BE              ;                       If we are a fugitive or a serious offender and we bump into a bounty hunter, they will become hostile and attack us (see bit #2)
 173++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are bounty hunters: Viper, Fer-de-lance
 174++C0BE              ;#2	Hostile flag        * 0 = not hostile  * 1 = hostile
 175++C0BE              ;                       Hostile ships will attack us on sight; there are quite a few of them
 176++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are hostile: Sidewinder, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Gecko, Cobra Mk I, Worm, Cobra Mk III, Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Moray, Thargoid, Thargon, Constrictor
 177++C0BE              ;#3	Pirate flag         * 0 = not a pirate * 1 = pirate
 178++C0BE              ;                       Hostile pirates will attack us on sight, but once we get inside the space station safe zone, they will stop
 179++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are pirates: Sidewinder, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Gecko, Cobra Mk I, Cobra Mk III, Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Moray, Thargoid
 180++C0BE              ;#4	Docking flag        * 0 = not docking * 1 = docking
 181++C0BE              ;                       Traders with their docking flag set fly towards the space station to try to dock, otherwise they aim for the planet
 182++C0BE              ;                       This flag is randomly set for traders when they are spawned
 183++C0BE              ;                       Ships that can be docking: Escape pod, Shuttle, Transporter, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Worm
 184++C0BE              ;#5	Innocent bystander  * 0 = normal * 1 = innocent bystander
 185++C0BE              ;                       If we attack an innocent ship within the space station safe zone, then the station will get angry with us and start spawning cops
 186++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are innocent bystanders: Shuttle, Transporter, Cobra Mk III, Python, Boa, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Cougar
 187++C0BE              ;#6	Cop flag            * 0 = not a cop * 1 = cop
 188++C0BE              ;                       If we destroy a cop, then we instantly become a fugitive (the Transporter isn't actually a cop, but it's clearly under police protection)
 189++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are cops: Viper, Transporter
 190++C0BE              ;#7	Scooped, docked, escape pod flag
 191++C0BE              ;                       For spawned ships, this flag indicates that the ship been scooped or has docked (bit 7 is always clear on spawning)
 192++C0BE              ;                       For blueprints, this flag indicates whether the ship type has an escape pod fitted, so it can launch it when in dire straits
 193++C0BE              ;                       Ships that have escape pods: Cobra Mk III, Python, Boa, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Viper, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Cobra Mk I, Cobra Mk III (pirate), Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Fer-de-lance

1478+ D703              ; Pitch and roll are 2 phases
1479+ D703              ; 1 - we apply our pitch and roll to the ship position
1480+ D703              ;       x -> x + alpha * (y - alpha * x)
1481+ D703              ;       y -> y - alpha * x - beta * z
1482+ D703              ;       z -> z + beta * (y - alpha * x - beta * z)
1483+ D703              ; which can be simplified as:
1484+ D703              ;       1. K2 = y - alpha * x
1485+ D703              ;       2. z = z + beta * K2
1486+ D703              ;       3. y = K2 - beta * z
1487+ D703              ;       4. x = x + alpha * y
1488+ D703              ; 2 - we apply our patch and roll to the ship orientation
1489+ D703              ;      Roll calculations:
1490+ D703              ;
1491+ D703              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - alpha * nosev_x_hi
1492+ D703              ;        nosev_x = nosev_x + alpha * nosev_y_hi
1493+ D703              ;      Pitch calculations:
1494+ D703              ;
1495+ D703              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - beta * nosev_z_hi
1496+ D703              ;        nosev_z = nosev_z + beta * nosev_y_hi
1497+ D703
1498+ D703

 207+ C290              ; -------------------------------------------------------------
 208+ C290              ; Sun Position    z = ((seed.d & 7) | 1)      shift left 16
 209+ C290              ;                 x = (seed.f & 3) shift left 16  | seed.f & 3 << 8 * -1 if seed f odd
 210+ C290              ;                 y    = sun x position
 211+ C290              ;
 212+ C290              CalculateSunWarpPositon:
 213+ C290 3A F2 82     .CalcZPosition:         ld      a,(WorkingSeeds+3)      ; seed d & 7
 214+ C293 E6 07                                and     %00000111               ; .
 215+ C295 F6 81                                or      %10000001               ; | 1
 216+ C297 32 18 C0     .SetZPosition:          ld      (SBnKzsgn),a            ; << 16 (i.e. load into z sign byte
 217+ C29A 21 00 00                             ld      hl, $0000               ; now set z hi and lo
 218+ C29D 22 16 C0                             ld      (SBnKzlo),hl            ;
 219+ C2A0 3A F4 82     .CalcXandYPosition:     ld      a,(WorkingSeeds+5)      ; seed f & 3
 220+ C2A3 E6 03                                and     %00000011               ; .
 221+ C2A5 47                                   ld      b,a
 222+ C2A6 3A F3 82                             ld      a,(WorkingSeeds+4)      ; get low bit of seed e
 223+ C2A9 E6 01                                and     %00000001
 224+ C2AB 1F                                   rra                             ; roll bi t0 into bit 7
 225+ C2AC B0                                   or      b                       ; now calc is f & 3 * -1 if seed e is odd
 226+ C2AD 32 12 C0     .SetXandYPosition:      ld      (SBnKxsgn),a            ; set into x and y sign byte
 227+ C2B0 32 15 C0                             ld      (SBnKysgn),a            ; .
 228+ C2B3 78                                   ld      a,b                     ; we want just seed f & 3 here
 229+ C2B4 32 11 C0                             ld      (SBnKxhi),a             ; set into x and y high byte
 230+ C2B7 32 14 C0                             ld      (SBnKyhi),a             ; .
 231+ C2BA                                      ZeroA
 231+ C2BA AF          >                        xor a

 525+ C4EC
 526+ C4EC              ; Pitch and roll are 2 phases
 527+ C4EC              ; 1 - we apply our pitch and roll to the ship position
 528+ C4EC              ;       x -> x + alpha * (y - alpha * x)
 529+ C4EC              ;       y -> y - alpha * x - beta * z
 530+ C4EC              ;       z -> z + beta * (y - alpha * x - beta * z)
 531+ C4EC              ; which can be simplified as:
 532+ C4EC              ;       1. K2 = y - alpha * x
 533+ C4EC              ;       2. z = z + beta * K2
 534+ C4EC              ;       3. y = K2 - beta * z
 535+ C4EC              ;       4. x = x + alpha * y
 536+ C4EC              ; 2 - we apply our patch and roll to the ship orientation
 537+ C4EC              ;      Roll calculations:
 538+ C4EC              ;
 539+ C4EC              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - alpha * nosev_x_hi
 540+ C4EC              ;        nosev_x = nosev_x + alpha * nosev_y_hi
 541+ C4EC              ;      Pitch calculations:
 542+ C4EC              ;
 543+ C4EC              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - beta * nosev_z_hi
 544+ C4EC              ;        nosev_z = nosev_z + beta * nosev_y_hi
 545+ C4EC
 546+ C4EC
 547+ C4EC                          INCLUDE "./Universe/Sun/SunApplyMyRollAndPitch.asm"

  13++C4EC              ;  3. y = K2 - beta * z
  14++C4EC              ;  4. x = x + alpha * y
  15++C4EC              ;.... or
  16++C4EC              ;  2. z = z + (beta * (y - alpha * x))
  17++C4EC              ;  3. y = (y - alpha * x) - (beta * z)
  18++C4EC              ;  4. x = x + (alpha * y)

  21++C4EC              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  22++C4EC              ; Sun version of pitch and roll is a 24 bit calculation 1 bit sign + 23 bit value
  23++C4EC              ; Need to write a test routine for roll and pitchs
  24++C4EC              ; Minsky Roll       Minsky Pitch
  25++C4EC              ;  y -= alpha * x    y -= beta * z
  26++C4EC              ;  x += alpha * y    z += beta * y
  27++C4EC              ; or once combined
  28++C4EC              ;   1. K2 = y - alpha * x
  29++C4EC              ;   2. z = z + beta * K2
  30++C4EC              ;   3. y = K2 - beta * z
  31++C4EC              ;   4. x = x + alpha * y
  32++C4EC              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  33++C4EC              ;	alpha = flight_roll / 256.0;
  34++C4EC              ;	beta = flight_climb / 256.0;
  35++C4EC              ;    k2 = y - alpha * x;
  36++C4EC              ;	z = z + beta * k2;
  37++C4EC              ;	y = k2 - z * beta;
  38++C4EC              ;	x = x + alpha * y;

 617+ C863              ; we only hit this if z is positive so we can ignore signs
 618+ C863              ; radius = 16384 / (z / 256): BBC Elite uses 24576 (on the same X / (Z / 256) scale as the projected centre), scaled to
 619+ C863              ; 2/3 as our view is 128 rows high against the BBC 192, so the size still grows in step with
 620+ C863              ; the position. Worked as 32768 / (z / 128) for an extra bit of precision: PlanetUpdateAndRender only draws when
 621+ C863              ; z sign < 48 and z >= 256, so z / 128 is 2..24575 and fits the 16 bit divisor. Any radius 1..248 (odd or even)
 622+ C863              ; so the planet grows a pixel at a time rather than jumping

 339+ E104 DD 21 38 E0  scan_keyboard:          ld		ix,RawKeys                      ; hl = table of raw IO port readings
 340+ E108 21 42 E0                             ld		hl,KeyAddrTab                   ; de = table of IO ports to read
 341+ E10B 0E 08                                ld		c,8                             ; 8 ports to ready
 342+ E10D 11 00 E0                             ld      de,Keys                         ; ix = table of key states from raw read
 343+ E110 7E           .PortReadLoop:          ld		a,(hl)							; Set up port to read as (hl)$FE
 344+ E111 DB FE                                in		a,($FE)							; read port to a
 345+ E113 DD 77 00                             ld      (ix+0),a                        ; save raw scan
 346+ E116 DD 23                                inc     ix
 347+ E118 23                                   inc		hl                              ; and ready for next read
 348+ E119 06 05        .ProcessInputBits:      ld		b,5								; loop all bits (there are only 5 keys to a group)
 349+ E11B 1F           .ProcessBitsLoop:       rra                                     ; shit bit 0 into carry
 350+ E11C 30 08                                jr      nc,.SetKeyPressed               ; low bit means it was pressed
 351+ E11E FD 6F                                ld      iyl,a
 352+ E120                                      ZeroA
 352+ E120 AF          >                        xor a
 353+ E121 C3 2E E1                             jp      .SetKey
 354+ E124 20 0B                                jr		nz,.SkipKeySet
 355+ E126 FD 6F        .SetKeyPressed:	        ld      iyl,a                           ; save current input byte
 356+ E128 1A                                   ld      a,(de)                          ; get current keystate
 357+ E129 FE 02                                cp      2
 358+ E12B 28 02                                jr      z,.AlreadyHeld
 359+ E12D 3C                                   inc     a                               ; and increment by 1 as its moved from previous state
 360+ E12E 12           .SetKey:                ld		(de),a				  	        ; save key Pressed state
 361+ E12F FD 7D        .AlreadyHeld:           ld      a,iyl                           ; and retrieve the current input byte
 362+ E131 13           .SkipKeySet:	        inc		de								; move to next key
 363+ E132 10 E7                                djnz	.ProcessBitsLoop				; Process all key group bits
 364+ E134 0D                                   dec     c                               ; thats one row of bits all processed
 365+ E135 20 D9                                jr      nz,.PortReadLoop				; Read next input port
 366+ E137              .ReadExtend0:           ; bits are set to 1 for press on the next register
 367+ E137                                      GetNextReg EXTENDED_KEYS_0_REGISTER
 367+ E137 01 3B 24    >            ld bc,$243B
 367+ E13A 3E B0       >            ld a,EXTENDED_KEYS_0_REGISTER
 367+ E13C ED 79       >            out (c),a
 367+ E13E 04          >            inc b
 367+ E13F ED 78       >            in a,(c)
 368+ E141 32 40 E0                             ld      (RawKeys+8),a                   ; save to extended slot
 369+ E144 06 08                                ld      b,8
 370+ E146 21 28 E0                             ld      hl,Keys + VK_SEMI
 371+ E149 5F                                   ld      e,a                             ; e now holds the raw keys for shifting
 372+ E14A CB 13        .ProcessExtend0:        rl      e                               ; shift bits left into carry for extended keys
 373+ E14C 38 04                                jr      c,.SetExtend0KeyPressed         ; if carry they key was pressedw
 374+ E14E              .Extend0NotPressed:     ZeroA
 374+ E14E AF          >                        xor a
 375+ E14F C3 58 E1                             jp      .SetExtend0Key
 376+ E152 7E           .SetExtend0KeyPressed:  ld      a,(hl)                          ; consider if key was already held down
 377+ E153 FE 02                                cp      2
 378+ E155 28 02                                jr      z,.Extend0AlreadyHeld
 379+ E157 3C                                   inc     a
 380+ E158 77           .SetExtend0Key:         ld      (hl),a
 381+ E159 23           .Extend0AlreadyHeld:    inc     hl
 382+ E15A 10 EE                                djnz    .ProcessExtend0
 383+ E15C              .ReadExtend1:           GetNextReg EXTENDED_KEYS_1_REGISTER
 383+ E15C 01 3B 24    >            ld bc,$243B
 383+ E15F 3E B1       >            ld a,EXTENDED_KEYS_1_REGISTER
 383+ E161 ED 79       >            out (c),a
 383+ E163 04          >            inc b
 383+ E164 ED 78       >            in a,(c)
 384+ E166 32 41 E0                             ld      (RawKeys+9),a                      ; save to extended slot
 385+ E169 06 08                                ld      b,8
 386+ E16B 21 30 E0                             ld      hl,Keys + VK_DELETE
 387+ E16E 5F                                   ld      e,a
 388+ E16F CB 13        .ProcessExtend1:        rl      e                                 ; shift bits left into carry for extended keys
 389+ E171 38 04                                jr      c,.SetExtend1KeyPressed
 390+ E173              .Extend1NotPressed:     ZeroA
 390+ E173 AF          >                        xor a
 391+ E174 C3 7D E1                             jp      .SetExtend1Key
 392+ E177 7E           .SetExtend1KeyPressed:  ld      a,(hl)
 393+ E178 FE 02                                cp      2
 394+ E17A 28 02                                jr      z,.Extend1AlreadyHeld
 395+ E17C 3C                                   inc     a
 396+ E17D 77           .SetExtend1Key:         ld      (hl),a
 397+ E17E 23           .Extend1AlreadyHeld:    inc     hl
 398+ E17F 10 EE                                djnz    .ProcessExtend1
 399+ E181 C9                                   ret

 293+ E23E 3A 57 82     .SetUpTone:             ld      a,(DELTA)
 294+ E241 A7                                   and     a
 295+ E242 CA 7D E2                             jp      z,.EngineOff    ; if speed is 0 the engine off as a = 0
 296+ E245 21 F3 08                             ld      hl,$08F3        ; base tone - delta * 15
 297+ E248 57                                   ld      d,a             ; we subtract as the tone is the

 310+ E262 3A 57 82     .SetUpNoise:            ld      a,(DELTA)       ; l = DELTA / 4
 311+ E265 CB 3F                                srl     a
 312+ E267 57                                   ld      d,a             ;
 313+ E268 CB 3F                                srl     a

   2+ 0000              ; Same signs add the magnitudes (the sign in bit 7 of B carries through), opposite signs subtract the smaller
   3+ 0000              ; magnitude from the larger and take that operand's sign. Never returns -0, overflow is not detected.
   4+ 0000              ; Destroys C and DE.

 113+ 08AE
 114+ 08AE              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 115+ 08AE              ; Ship version of ApplyMyRollAndPitchIX with an extra fraction byte per axis.
 116+ 08AE              ; With roll / pitch rates of only 1..2 / 256 per frame, alpha * x truncated to whole raw units is 0 for any |x| below
 117+ 08AE              ; 128..256 raw, so nearby ships close to the centre of view never moved when the player rolled. Here each axis is
 118+ 08AE              ; worked as a 32 bit 2's complement value (raw * 256 + fraction) and the fraction is kept between frames.
 119+ 08AE              ; Products are truncated towards zero so the Minsky rotation has no drift in either direction.
 120+ 08AE              ; ix = 24 bit lead sign position (x, y, z each lo, hi, sign), iy = 3 fraction bytes (x, y, z). ix and iy preserved
 121+ 08AE              ; Its work variables (RPX32 .. RPSign) are in general_variables.asm, not here: this bank is in slot 0 and writes to
 122+ 08AE              ; $0000-$3FFF can be going to layer 2, so variables in this bank read back as garbage
 123+ 08AE
 124+ 08AE              ; 32 bit 2's complement value at dest = position axis at ix+ixoff (lo, hi, sign) * 256 + fraction at iy+iyoff
 125+ 08AE              RPLoadAxis:                 MACRO   dest, ixoff, iyoff
 126+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(iy+iyoff)
 127+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (dest),a
 128+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(ix+ixoff)
 129+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (dest+1),a
 130+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(ix+ixoff+1)
 131+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (dest+2),a
 132+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(ix+ixoff+2)
 133+ 08AE ~                                        ld      b,a
 134+ 08AE ~                                        and     $7F
 135+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (dest+3),a
 136+ 08AE ~                                        bit     7,b
 137+ 08AE ~                                        jr      z,.Positive
 138+ 08AE ~                                        ld      hl,dest
 139+ 08AE ~                                        call    RPNeg32
 140+ 08AE ~            .Positive:
 141+ 08AE                                          ENDM
 142+ 08AE
 143+ 08AE              ; position axis at ix+ixoff and fraction at iy+iyoff = 32 bit 2's complement value at src (src is left as |src|)
 144+ 08AE              RPSaveAxis:                 MACRO   src, ixoff, iyoff
 145+ 08AE ~                                        ld      b,0
 146+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(src+3)
 147+ 08AE ~                                        and     a
 148+ 08AE ~                                        jp      p,.Positive
 149+ 08AE ~                                        ld      hl,src
 150+ 08AE ~                                        call    RPNeg32
 151+ 08AE ~                                        ld      b,$80
 152+ 08AE ~            .Positive:                  ld      a,(src)
 153+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (iy+iyoff),a
 154+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(src+1)
 155+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (ix+ixoff),a
 156+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(src+2)
 157+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (ix+ixoff+1),a
 158+ 08AE ~                                        ld      a,(src+3)
 159+ 08AE ~                                        or      b
 160+ 08AE ~                                        ld      (ix+ixoff+2),a
 161+ 08AE                                          ENDM

 164+ 08E9 E6 7F       >                            and     $7F

 211+ 0A13
 212+ 0A13              ; RPProd = (hl) * a / 256, (hl) = 32 bit 2's complement, a = lead sign S7 rotator, truncated towards zero
 213+ 0A13              ; uses a, bc, de, hl
 214+ 0A13 32 78 81     RPMulRot:                   ld      (RPRot),a
 215+ 0A16 11 70 81                                 ld      de,RPAbs                ; RPAbs = |(hl)|
 216+ 0A19 01 04 00                                 ld      bc,4                    ; .
 217+ 0A1C ED B0                                    ldir                            ; .
 218+ 0A1E 3A 73 81                                 ld      a,(RPAbs+3)             ; .
 219+ 0A21 47                                       ld      b,a                     ; b bit 7 = sign of (hl)
 220+ 0A22 A7                                       and     a                       ; .
 221+ 0A23 F2 2C 0A                                 jp      p,.Positive             ; .
 222+ 0A26 21 70 81                                 ld      hl,RPAbs                ; .
 223+ 0A29 CD 77 0A                                 call    RPNeg32                 ; .
 224+ 0A2C 3A 78 81     .Positive:                  ld      a,(RPRot)               ; sign of the result
 225+ 0A2F A8                                       xor     b                       ; .
 226+ 0A30 E6 80                                    and     $80                     ; .
 227+ 0A32 32 79 81                                 ld      (RPSign),a              ; .
 228+ 0A35 3A 78 81                                 ld      a,(RPRot)               ; c = |rotator|
 229+ 0A38 E6 7F                                    and     $7F                     ; .
 230+ 0A3A 4F                                       ld      c,a                     ; .
 231+ 0A3B 3A 70 81                                 ld      a,(RPAbs)               ; |v| * c / 256: byte 0 of the product is dropped
 232+ 0A3E 57                                       ld      d,a                     ; .
 233+ 0A3F 59                                       ld      e,c                     ; .
 234+ 0A40 ED 30                                    mul     de                      ; .
 235+ 0A42 42                                       ld      b,d                     ; b = carry in to byte 1
 236+ 0A43 3A 71 81                                 ld      a,(RPAbs+1)             ; .
 237+ 0A46 57                                       ld      d,a                     ; .
 238+ 0A47 59                                       ld      e,c                     ; .
 239+ 0A48 ED 30                                    mul     de                      ; .
 240+ 0A4A 7B                                       ld      a,e                     ; .
 241+ 0A4B 80                                       add     a,b                     ; .
 242+ 0A4C 32 74 81                                 ld      (RPProd),a              ; .
 243+ 0A4F 42                                       ld      b,d                     ; (mul leaves the carry flag alone)
 244+ 0A50 3A 72 81                                 ld      a,(RPAbs+2)             ; .
 245+ 0A53 57                                       ld      d,a                     ; .
 246+ 0A54 59                                       ld      e,c                     ; .
 247+ 0A55 ED 30                                    mul     de                      ; .
 248+ 0A57 7B                                       ld      a,e                     ; .
 249+ 0A58 88                                       adc     a,b                     ; .

   5+ 0B51 ~                                    ld      a,h
   6+ 0B51 ~                                    or      l
   7+ 0B51 ~                                    or      d

   9+ 0B51 ~                                    ld      a,1

  22+ 0B51 ~                                    sla     h

   1+ 0DA7              ; ix = pointer to orientation matrix, each value a 16 bit lead sign word with 1.0 = $6000 (96 in the hi byte)
   2+ 0DA7              ; ix data structure needs to be
   3+ 0DA7              ;       X          y            Z
   4+ 0DA7              ; side +00 , +01   +02 , +03    +04 , +05
   5+ 0DA7              ; roof +06 , +07   +08 , +09    +10 , +11
   6+ 0DA7              ; nose +12 , +13   +14 , +15    +16 , +17
   7+ 0DA7              ;
   8+ 0DA7              ; Re-orthonormalises the matrix against drift (Elite TIDY), working on the hi bytes as Normalise16IX does:
   9+ 0DA7              ;   1. nose = nose / |nose|
  10+ 0DA7              ;   2. make roof perpendicular to nose: pick the nose axis k with the largest |nose_k| (>= 96/sqrt(3) once normalised,
  11+ 0DA7              ;      so the divide is well conditioned and roof moves the least) and set roof_k = -(nose_a * roof_a + nose_b * roof_b) / nose_k
  12+ 0DA7              ;   3. roof = roof / |roof|
  13+ 0DA7              ;   4. side = (nose x roof) / 96, then side = side / |side|
  14+ 0DA7              ; ix is preserved, uses the banked maths routines so MathsBankedFns must be paged in
  15+ 0DA7 DD E5        TidyOrientation:        push    ix

   4+ 0EBD              sqrtHL:
   5+ 0EBD              ;Input: HL
   6+ 0EBD              ;Output: A is the integer square root of HL
